top.title: Luck turns around for Golden Knights in shootout win over Jets
top.description: Nov 21, 2026; Winnipeg, Manitoba, CAN; Vegas Golden Knights center William Karlsson (71) score the winning goal in the shoot out on Winnipeg Jets goaltender Stuart Skinner (74) at Canada Life Centre. WINNIPEG—Heading back on the road, the Vegas Golden Knights needed any sort of momentum to get their season back on track. Sitting in second place in the Pacific Division by a comfortable margin, the Golden Knights were hardly in danger of losing their place in the standings. However, four straight losses to close out a five-game homestand undoubtedly left a sour taste in the mouths of players, coaches and fans alike. Between the loss to the last-place Vancouver Canucks, three losses last regulation and two straight third-period collapses against the Dallas Stars, the Golden Knights were in need of anything to stem the tide against them. Now on a road trip that will go beyond Thanksgiving, the Golden Knights finally got a break from their recent stretch of hard luck, securing a 5-4 shootout victory over the Winnipeg Jets to snap their losing streak. The Jets would force the Golden Knights on the back foot from the opening shot, as captain Adam Lowry would deflect Elias Salomonsson’s shot past Carter Hart to open the scoring in favor of the home side. However, the Golden Knights would come roaring back, starting with a clean faceoff win from Jack Eichel leading to a quick shot from Brett Howden that Winnipeg goaltender Stuart Skinner was unable to see. Less than 90 seconds later, Trevor Connelly and Mitch Marner continued to showcase their impressive chemistry, with the latter collecting a pass from the former and eventually potting in his own rebound for Vegas’ first lead of the night. The lead would not last through the end of the first period, as Eichel would cough up the puck in the neutral zone in the final minutes to lead to a tying goal from Jets rookie forward Viggo Bjorck. In the second period, controversy would strike during a Golden Knights power play when the net would come off its moorings before Tomas Hertl’s shot made it in. However, the referees would rule that Victor Olofsson was knocked into the net by Jets forward Alex Iafallo, counting the goal in favor of Vegas. The Winnipeg crowd’s vitriol would quickly turn into euphoria, as forward Mark Scheifele would pass Jets legend Dale Hawerchuk on the franchise’s all-time record with his 380th goal to tie the game at three. Kyle Connor would push the Jets back into the lead but, with less than four minutes remaining, a smart play from Hertl would give Ivan Barbashev time and space in the slot to sink a perfect shot past Skinner to push the Golden Knights to overtime for the third straight game. Despite some struggles, Hart would settle in with some key saves in the third period and overtime to preserve a point and keep the Golden Knights in it. top.description: Tornike Kvaratskhelia: Man United battling Arsenal, Chelsea for Georgian winger Manchester United’s pursuit of a talented young winger, who is fast earning admirers across the continent, is unlikely to be a walk in the park. The Red Devils were keen to bolster the left-forward role over the summer, but their failure to offload Marcus Rashford , who returned from a fruitful loan spell at Barcelona, perhaps hurt their plans. The Englishman has failed to replicate last season’s form and the Premier League giants have lacked threat on the wings. With Matheus Cunha hardly faring any better, there has been talk of further reinforcements for the position at the turn of the year. While United will be looking for an immediate fix for the position, they are also likely to have an eye out for the future. INEOS have targeted several talented young footballers since their arrival in 2024 to build a backbone for the future and it now appears that they have unearthed another gem, this time in Georgia. top.description: Lyndon Faulkner officially takes over as WRU chair in Decemeber [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Former Wales captain Jonathan Davies says new Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) chairman Lyndon Faulkner is the man to turn Welsh rugby around. The former Newport and Pontypool forward, who will take over from Richard Collier-Keywood , attends his first WRU annual general meeting (AGM) on Sunday. He has already promised to review everything including the controversial plan to cut a men's professional side by 2028, Faulkner has forged a highly successful business career in the United States of America. The 66-year-old also has a Welsh rugby background as the nephew of former Wales rugby prop Charlie Faulkner, who was yesterday inducted into World Rugby's hall of fame alongside Bobby Windsor and Graham Price - the famed Pontypool front-row. Former Wales fly-half Davies, who called for the WRU board to resign before Faulkner's appointment, believes the new will chair galvanise Welsh rugby off the field when he officially starts his role next month. “I believe the chair is a good guy and he has the opportunity to change things and he will make them,” said Davies. “He is a successful businessman, but he is a rugby man." Davies has described the problems at the WRU as similar to Manchester United. “When I look at Man United, I also look at the WRU," Davies told BBC 5 Live sport. "When Man United changed and brought the bankers in there was no football knowledge and the same has happened in Welsh rugby." The former Wales captain said decisions that have been made by the union have been purely financial, and not rugby ones. “Lyndon is the right man and will make the necessary changes in the WRU to give these guys a better platform," Davies added. “It’s not going to happen overnight and if we don‘t make these changes we will be in tier two for a long time.” WRU names businessman Faulkner as new chairman WRU is to blame for current mess - Davies Jonathan Davies is a former dual-code rugby international [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Davies believes the WRU needs to help the players who earlier this month inspired the nation with a first victory against New Zealand in 73 years, a match played in front of just over 55,000 fans. “I heard Dewi Lake say something before the New Zealand game and I felt really sorry for the players," said Davies. “He said because the attendance was low that was down to them. top.title: Five quick takeaways from Las Vegas GP
top.description: Motorsport photo Las Vegas gets the pack race it craved In America's artificial entertainment capital, F1 put the most artificial and entertaining spectacle. How fitting. The yo-yo racing from the early days of the 2026 season was back on full display, with the lack of electric energy available on the Strip's mile long straight bring back battery driven overtaking. For a while it felt like we were watching the Indy 500, with the top cars trading the lead without being able to break away from the rest of the pack. It led to numerous position changes and plenty of wheel-to-wheel races, much to the delight of the soldout crowd and event officials. It's certainly not for everyone, but you can't deny there was something to watch. And it was certainly a much better watch than the Madring's Spanish Grand Prix. - Fil Cleeren Ferrari in meltdown as Hamilton and Leclerc clash again Ferrari came into Las Vegas with two clear objectives: Try to win (naturally) and try to lockdown second place in the F1 world constructors’ championship. While the first target was going to be a tall order given the Scuderia’s lack of engine punch on the long Las Vegas straights, not losing more than 10 points to Red Bull was entirely realistic to second P2. But then the unsolved objectives reared up once again. Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc seem unable to race each other as team-mates. That much was evident in Mexico as they cost each other the win, but clear-the-air talks were meant to have solved all that in Brazil. Two weeks later, it is worse than ever. Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Hamilton vented his fury at Leclerc for fighting him in the pack during the opening act of the Las Vegas GP slipstreaming, battery-boosting ‘race’, with the Monegasque on the scene when he ran off the road and kept ahead of Lando Norris to pick up a 10-second penalty. After having to serve his penalty a lap into the safety car period, in order not to hold up Leclerc who was behind him, the pair re-engaged their on-track disagreements and it was Leclerc’s turn to make the error. But this time he clattered into his team-mate, spinning Hamilton around, and earning himself a 10s penalty. top.title: F1 Las Vegas GP: Max Verstappen wins thriller as Ferraris come to blows
top.description: Motorsport photo Max Verstappen won an eventful Las Vegas Grand Prix, holding off both Mercedes as Formula 1’s novel ‘yo-yo’ racing returned – with no Silver Arrow on the eventual podium. With qualifying pacesetter Kimi Antonelli taking a five-place grid penalty for exceeding his engine allocation, Max Verstappen inherited pole position and retained the lead from George Russell at the start with an unchanged top five: Lando Norris, Isack Hadjar and Arvid Lindblad followed – though Hadjar swiftly found a way past the McLaren on lap one. The only top-10 driver starting on mediums, Antonelli lost two spots to the Alpines at lights out, finding himself eighth ahead of the Ferraris, who were out in Q2 – though Franco Colapinto would soon collapse from seventh to 10th, then out of the points-paying positions. Verstappen couldn’t break away from Russell, and the Briton briefly snatched the lead away on lap two before the Dutchman immediately responded. Russell couldn’t attack the leader again and was instead overtaken by the sister Red Bull car. Now it was these two trading places… until Lindblad remarkably overtook Norris and Russell in quick succession, even though he could not hold the Mercedes off. Meanwhile, Hadjar was pressuring Verstappen for the lead but had to deal with Russell’s attacks. “We need to not lose time as a team,” the Frenchman was told. “Can he stop defending?” he inquired about his team-mate’s driving. Hadjar briefly took the lead soon after, though he dropped to third moments later. On lap 10, the top 10 cars still lay within four seconds. Russell momentarily retook the lead (again) as Pierre Gasly fought to third, though he couldn’t hold off Hadjar for long. There were no changes among the top four for a moment, but Norris’ collapse continued as he ended up outside the top 10. Russell took the lead back on laps 14 and 18, but this was again Turn 14 moves with Verstappen sweeping back past on the start/finish straight. The second time, Hadjar snuck by in second. Meanwhile, the Ferraris were battling both their rivals and among themselves for seventh place. Charles Leclerc called on his team-mate to “be careful with this squeezing”; Lewis Hamilton said the sister car should “back the f**k off” – and copped a 10-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage. (AP) — Kate Harpring scored 20 points, Achol Akot added 16 and No. 24 North Carolina used two runs in the second half on Saturday to defeat Alabama 78-64 at the WBCA Showcase. The 16th and final lead change came during a 13-0 run to end the third quarter. Harping hit a pair of 3s and a 3 from Laila Hull at the buzzer gave the Tar Heels a 60-50 lead. Hull hit another 3 after the Crimson Tide got with seven points midway through the fourth quarter, starting a 10-0 run capped by a 3-pointer from Nyla Brooks that made it 76-59 with less than 2 minutes to go. Brooks added 14 points for the Tar Heels (4-2), who went 12 of 28 from the 3-point line and shot 46% overall to overcome a 4 of 11 showing at the foul line. Ace Austin had 15 points for the Crimson Tide (6-2). Alayna West added 13 points off the bench and Aaliyah Roberson scored 11. The Tar Heels scored the first nine points of the game but the Crimson Tide scrapped back to lead 38-36 at the half. top.description: The Boston Celtics were back in action on Saturday night, looking to snap a two-game skid and did so with a much different lineup thatn their normal go-to starters. Jayson Tatum, Derrick White, and Mitchell Robinson all missed the game, which allowed for Payton Pritchard, Hugo Gonzalez, and Sam Hauser to crrack the starting lineup, and this game against Sacramento had plenty of challenges. Just as they did in their last game, the Celtics jumped out to an early first half lead, but a rough third quarter allowed the Kings to get back into the game, and took the game down to the wire. In the end, it was the second half which led to the demise of the Celtics, and they'll need to figure it out quickly on the first night of a back-to-back for the weekend. Here's a quick recap of the Celtics coming up short against the Sacramento Kings , leading to their third straight loss. Final score: Sacramento Kings 97, Boston Celtics 96 Keys to the game: Different looking lineup: With multiple starters out for the game, it allowed for not only new starters but for others to step up with more opportunities, which is what veteran Mike Conley did throughout the night. Conley had 19 points off the bench for Boston, while Neemias Queta and Sam Hauser combined for 29 points between them to help the starting unit. Payton Pritchard and Paul George struggled in this game, which hurt the flow of the offense without Jayson Tatum and Derrick White. top.title: 'They couldn't live with it!' - Dominic Calvert-Lewin revels in Stamford Bridge rout as Chelsea crumble against Leeds United
top.description: Chelsea FC v Leeds United - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Dominic Calvert-Lewin urged his Leeds United team-mates to savour their first Stamford Bridge triumph since 1999 after dismantling Chelsea 4-1 in the Premier League. The in-form striker converted a crucial second-half penalty and insisted Xabi Alonso's hosts simply could not handle Leeds' relentless intensity. Calvert-Lewin relishes long-awaited Bridge triumph Dominic Calvert-Lewin called on Leeds United to savour their 4-1 Premier League demolition of Chelsea after helping the Whites secure their first victory at Stamford Bridge since 1999. The striker rattled home a pivotal second-half penalty between Noah Okafor's brace before substitute Brenden Aaronson added a stoppage-time fourth. Celebrations erupted inside the away end and visiting dressing room as Leeds climbed up to sixth in the table . "Great feeling," Calvert-Lewin said. "I think you can see it at the end, the way we celebrated it. It's always great to win in the Premier League, especially away from home in a place like Stamford Bridge, so I think you have to enjoy it." Relentless intensity overwhelms Alonso's Chelsea Leeds fell behind midway through the first half when Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead on his full debut, only for Okafor to equalise within three minutes. Rather than fading after the interval, Daniel Farke's men stepped up their pressing, won a penalty when a shot struck Morgan Rogers high on the arm, and blew the Blues away. "We expected them to probably come out with a bit more of a reaction, and we started the second half exactly the same as we started the first, which was intensity," Calvert-Lewin explained. "I don't think they could live with it today, and that was reflected in the scoreline." Peak fitness fuels striker's confident streak Calvert-Lewin proved a constant aerial menace throughout the contest, rattling Emiliano Martinez's crossbar with an early header before dispatching his spot-kick into the bottom corner. Fresh from winning in Madrid with England during the international break, the forward credited his physical rhythm for his commanding display. "I'm feeling comfortable in my body at the moment and really enjoying my football," Calvert-Lewin revealed. "And for me, when I feel like that, going onto a football pitch, I feel like I can play against anybody, so I'm full of confidence at the moment. A great seven days and a great result coming back in." Momentum builds for top-six contenders The victory capped an unforgettable week for Calvert-Lewin and underlined Leeds' growing credentials under Farke as they moved into sixth place ahead of the weekend's remaining fixtures. With Okafor clinical in front of goal and the squad brimming with belief, Leeds carry formidable momentum into the busy winter schedule. For Chelsea, meanwhile, defeat leaves Alonso searching for answers before the Blues travel to Nottingham Forest next Friday night.

top.title: Spurs star Victor Wembanyama drops tough ‘stat padding’ declaration after dropping 50 on Pelicans
top.description: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Spurs star Victor Wembanyama drops tough ‘stat padding’ declaration after dropping 50 on Pelicans appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Victor Wembanyama put together one of the most dominant performances of the NBA season on Saturday night , but the San Antonio Spurs star refused to take himself too seriously afterward. Wembanyama erupted for 50 points, 19 rebounds, five blocks and four steals as the Spurs cruised to a 114-91 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans at Frost Bank Center. When asked during his postgame interview how special it was to reach such a rare threshold, the 22-year-old offered a playful jab at the rest of the league. “It is very special. But unlike many of my peers, I’m not very good at stat-padding. So, I haven’t reached it yet,” Wembanyama said, via the Spurs X account. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "Unlike many of my peers, i'm not very good at statpadding" Victor Wembanyama after his 50-point outburst 😳 (via @spurs ) pic.twitter.com/kdNFR3BpYR — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 22, 2026 The comment was classic Wembanyama, whose dry sense of humor has become a regular part of his postgame routine. He finished just one rebound shy of a 50-point, 20-rebound night. There was nothing padded about his numbers, though. Wembanyama shot an efficient 20-of-29 from the field, including 5-of-11 from beyond the arc, and San Antonio outscored New Orleans by 35 points with him on the floor. The Spurs led by as many as 29 points. The outing also cemented his place in the history books . Wembanyama became just the fourth player in NBA history with at least 50 points, 15 rebounds and five blocks in a game, joining Wilt Chamberlain, Anthony Davis and Bob McAdoo. He has now done it twice this month, after putting up 52 points, 24 rebounds and eight blocks against the Dallas Mavericks on Nov. 4. Wembanyama also joined David Robinson as the only players to record multiple 50-point, five-block games since blocks became an official stat in 1973-74. Stephon Castle added 19 points and hit five 3-pointers for the Spurs, while De’Aaron Fox dished out 10 assists. Jeremiah Fears paced the Pelicans with 29 points, and Jordan Poole scored 25. San Antonio improved to 14-3 with the victory and has won 12 of its last 13 games . If this is what Wembanyama looks like when he isn’t chasing numbers, the rest of the league should be worried about what happens when he actually tries. The disagreement over the position of his son, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, has moved from the church’s internal leadership structure to the courts, with competing claims over the late founder’s wishes, the church’s constitution and the authority of its Board of Trustees. The trustees said their decision followed a review of the church’s succession arrangements and a video recording made by the late Taiwo Odukoya in December 2021, in which he allegedly named Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor. Odukoya’s wife, Pastor Bimbo, a co-founder of the church, had earlier died in a plane crash. According to the trustees, the late founder proposed that Jimmy serve as Areogun’s administrative assistant and head of the church’s youth ministry. They said the recording was made available to them in December 2025 and was not presented when Jimmy was appointed senior pastor in September 2023. The trustees subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader, pending consultations and the establishment of a substantive leadership structure. The marriage followed the end of Jimmy’s previous union with Oluwakemi Banjoko, whom he married in London in March 2013. The couple have two children. nigeria.title: Why construction could become Africa’s key technology, investment opportunity
nigeria.description: By Jimoh Razaq For years, Africa’s technology ecosystem has concentrated much of its entrepreneurial energy, investment capital and innovation around fintech, e-commerce, mobility, telecommunications and entertainment. But there is another industry with enormous economic significance, deeply entrenched inefficiencies and a largely untapped opportunity for technological transformation: construction. It is an industry that builds our homes, roads, hospitals, schools, factories, power infrastructure and cities. It employs millions of people, supports extensive manufacturing and distribution networks, moves significant volumes of capital and sits at the centre of economic development. Yet much of its operational infrastructure remains fragmented, manual and inefficient. While technology has transformed how people transfer money, order food, book transportation and access entertainment, the processes through which buildings and infrastructure are planned, financed, procured and delivered remain remarkably difficult to coordinate. This is not simply an operational inconvenience. It is a massive economic opportunity. nigeria.title: PSHAN, WHO urge increased private investment to rescue Nigeria’s healthcare system
nigeria.description: By Matthew Johnson The Private Sector Health Alliance of Nigeria (PSHAN) and the World Health Organisation (WHO) have called for increased private sector investment and stronger public-private partnerships to address persistent challenges confronting Nigeria’s healthcare system. The organisations said government alone could not shoulder the responsibility of transforming the health sector, stressing that sustained private sector investment was critical to improving healthcare delivery, strengthening infrastructure and achieving universal health coverage. The call was made at the 2026 PSHAN Annual Gala and Awards Night held in Lagos on November 20, with the theme, “Legacy Builders: Honouring the Visionaries of the Nigerian Healthcare System.” Speaking at the event, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of PSHAN, Dr. Tinuola Akinbolagbe, said the alliance was working to position the private sector at the centre of Nigeria’s health development through strategic partnerships, investment, innovation and institutional strengthening. She said PSHAN was seeking to move beyond fragmented private sector interventions towards coordinated investments capable of strengthening health systems and delivering measurable and sustainable outcomes. According to her, meaningful progress in healthcare requires shared responsibility and collaboration across different sectors. “As we look towards 2027 and beyond, our ambition is to move from fragmented contributions by the private sector to coordinated investment, from isolated interventions to stronger health systems, and from good intentions to measurable, sustainable outcomes,” she said. Akinbolagbe explained that the theme of the event was designed to celebrate individuals, institutions and organisations whose courage, leadership, innovation and commitment had contributed to shaping the future of healthcare in Nigeria. In his keynote address, former President of the African Development Bank Group and Executive Chairman of the Global Africa Investment Summit, Dr. Akinwumi Adesina, described healthcare as an investment in human capital and essential economic infrastructure rather than merely social sector expenditure. Speaking on the theme, “Health as Wealth: Mobilising African Leadership and Capital to Build Sustainable Health Systems,” Adesina said a healthy population was fundamental to productivity, innovation, economic competitiveness and national prosperity. He maintained that no country could achieve sustainable wealth without a healthy population, insisting that investment in healthcare was essential to building a productive workforce and inclusive economy. Adesina called for stronger partnerships between government and the private sector, noting that government alone could not finance and deliver the transformation required in the country’s healthcare system. nigeria.title: Anambra’s Ekwulobia flyover to be commissioned November 27
nigeria.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Anambra State Executive Council has fixed November 27, 2026, for the formal commissioning and opening of the Ekwulobia flyover constructed by the administration of Governor Chukwuma Soludo. The flyover is strategically located at a junction that previously experienced serious traffic challenges, particularly during festive periods when vehicular movement increases significantly. Rising from its meeting in Awka, the State Executive Council directed that all necessary arrangements be made to ensure a successful and hitch-free commissioning. However, it did not disclose who would perform the ceremony. The state Commissioner for Information and Value Reorientation, Dr Law Mefor, described the flyover as one of the flagship urban regeneration projects of the Soludo administration. He said the project stood alongside the transformation of Okpoko, formerly regarded as the biggest urban slum in the South-East, into an area characterised by improved infrastructure, order and human dignity. “These projects underscore Governor Soludo’s irreversible commitment to building a liveable, prosperous and smart mega-city in Anambra State,” Mefor said. Meanwhile, the Council resolved to move the state’s Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) drive from moral suasion to full enforcement, including the prosecution of tax evaders, to maximise the state’s revenue potential. It consequently urged residents, business owners and other taxpayers to pay their taxes and levies promptly to avoid the consequences of enforcement, particularly prosecution. According to the Council, no modern state can be built on voluntary compliance alone, stressing that payment of taxes is a civic responsibility. “Anambra will enforce it fairly and firmly,” the Council said. I pray that God Almighty repose their souls and comfort their families,” he said. Meanwhile, Governor Douye Diri has visited the scene of the accident and is expected to initiate a probe into the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. entertainment.description: A thoughtful young woman sits in a relaxed pose in a serene bedroom, reflecting peacefully. Photo credit: Alex Green/Pexels. I lost someone recently, and since then, I have found myself revisiting little moments, conversations and encounters I probably would not have given much thought to otherwise. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? Why did we have to start talking, sharing experiences and becoming familiar with each other again, only for him to die shortly afterwards? Why him? Why at that particular time? entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. However, I believe it is the responsibility of an award of this repute to look beyond the most visible names and recognise the best African music released within its eligibility period. A song should not earn a nomination simply because it is popular or has enjoyed international success. sports.title: Ospreys legends set to turn out to honour Tipuric
sports.description: Justin Tipuric gave up the Ospreys captaincy in 2024 with Jac Morgan taking over [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Welsh rugby fans will have a chance to pay tribute to Ospreys and Wales legend Justin Tipuric at St Helen's in Swansea on Sunday (14:30 GMT). An Ospreys legends vs Trebanos XV event will see Tipuric's only professional side take on his village club. The Ospreys legends squad includes former flanker Tipuric joined by fellow ex-Wales internationals Alun Wyn Jones, Shane Williams, James Hook, Richard Hibbard, Ian Gough, Scott Baldwin, Duncan Jones and Huw Bennett, while former back-rower and current Dragons head coach Filo Tiatia has also signed up. While Tipuric has been named in the Ospreys squad, he is expected to play for both sides. Tipuric lines ups among Ospreys legends Alun Wyn Jones and Justin Tipuric both retired from international rugby on the same day before the 2023 World Cup [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Tipuric retired at the end of the 2024-25 season to become Ospreys' defence coach. He was due to have a farewell home match at the old Swansea.com Stadium ground against Dragons in May 2025, but missed the match after picking up a pectoral injury against Lyon earlier that month. "There was a bit of a stick from a couple of the Trebanos guys saying they came down with a lot of the juniors to watch, but I wasn't even playing," said Tipuric. Ospreys have organised this occasion so fans can see Tipuric's famous blue scrum cap one more time on the rugby field. "The Ospreys said once we have our stadium done at St Helen's they wanted to make sure I had a game," added Tipuric. "Until I saw us kick off at St Helen's I didn't think I would see that happen because for the 20 years I've been involved, I've seen about five or six different plans. "I thought they had forgotten about it, so I didn't have to play, but they have been amazing with Richard Lancaster [Ospreys managing director] and so many people working behind the scenes." Shane Williams scored 58 tries in 87 internationals for Wales [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Modest man insists event is not about him The event does not have the Tipuric name in the title because the player himself was not keen on the spotlight. His insistence this is not labelled a testimonial match or a celebration of his career underlines how humble the flanker was during his playing days. Tipuric was always happier speaking about others than himself. His modesty off the field was matched by his brilliance on it. "It is definitely not about me, this is something for Ospreys, Trebanos and the fans," said Tipuric. "There are matches for the Trebanos juniors starting at 9am so they can get to play on the St Helen's pitch. "For the match itself, it will just be great to get people back in the building who have put an Ospreys jersey on during the last 20 years. "It's something we've never done before so that is quite special especially, hopefully, for the Ospreys fans, who have been amazing to me throughout my career."

sports.title: Islanders 3, Red Wings 2: Palat pair overcomes post luck
sports.description: A thousand games and a thousand hugs. | NHLI via Getty Images The Islanders banked another two points against an opponent they should beat, riding Ondrej Palat’s two goals to a 3-2 over the Red Wings in Detroit. Despite a good effort — certainly better than a couple nights ago in Winnipeg — it looked like things might not go their way when they were hitting posts (including Mathew Barzal, twice) while the Red Wings held a 1-0 lead thanks to a fortunate Joe Louis Little Caesar’s Whatever Arena end boards. But Palat scored midway through the second to tie it at 1-1, Simon Holmstrom finished off a broken 4-on-2 early i the third to give them the lead, and Ilya Sorokin made a sterling save to preserve the lead shortly before Palat extended it to 3-1. Alex DeBrincat, who is toiling away to honor his commitment to the Red Wings’ perpetual rebuild, scored his eighth of the season to make it close again with under seven minutes to go. Holmstrom’s goal, by the way, was his tenth. [ NHL Gamecenter | Game Summary | Event Summary | Natural Stat Trick ] It was a satisfying outcome for Casey Cizikas’ 1,000th regular season NHL game, complete with two goals from his fourth-line mate Palat. The 1,000 gamer also had a big shot block on Moritz Seider as time wound down to help seal the win. In addition to making a suite available for his family and friends who were in attendance, the Red Wings also gave him a Jumbotron salute during a TV stoppage. That drew a visit and embrace from Ben Chiarot, who fought Brayden Schenn a period later after the Wings defenseman roughed up Matthew Schaefer. (And that came after Chiarot got a roughing penalty for doing similar to Victor Eklund earlier in the period.) With the win, the Islanders keep pace in the wild card hunt, two points (27) behind current holders Florida (29), and with two games in hand. Up Next The Islanders return home to host the Leafs on Monday, the Blues on Wednesday and the Jets on Friday. Until then, find yourself someone who hugs you like Casey Cizikas hugs his victorious goalies.

science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". science.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. But the company had never attempted a Ship catch, which is a taller order, given how much faster and farther Starship upper stages fly. So snagging Ship on the first try was a very big deal, according to Musk. "Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," he told Baker and Gracias on Wednesday. The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket comes back to its launch tower for a "chopsticks" catch on Nov. 14, 2026, during the vehicle's 15th test flight. science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
science.description: null Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the solar system's innermost planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Today's orbital insertion is the latest milestone in BepiColombo's Mercury arrival phase, which is expected to take about six months in total. Arrival began on Sept. 3, when the MTM released MPO and Mio. The two orbiters remain connected today; they won't separate until Dec. 9 or thereabouts. Shortly thereafter, Mio will settle into its final orbit, a highly elliptical path that will take it over Mercury's poles. MPO is also destined for a polar orbit, though a much less elliptical one than Mio's; the ESA probe will conduct a series of engine burns before finally getting there on March 10, 2027. BepiColombo won't start doing science work until April 6, 2027. The two probes will gather complementary data from their two different vantage points, shedding a great deal of light on a mysterious world. "The mission will study all aspects of Mercury, from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind , to its internal structure with its large iron core, and the origin of the planet’s magnetic field," ESA officials wrote in a BepiColombo mission description . "The data will enable scientists to understand more about the origin and evolution of a planet located close to its parent star, and a better understanding of the overall evolution of our solar system," they added.

science.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
science.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers. science.description: null On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station. Today, the I nternational Space Station is about the size of a football field and typically hosts up to seven crewmembers. But back in 1998, it was a pretty tight squeeze. science.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
science.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.

It doesn't seem likely they'll journey to the stars anytime soon — you can't really do cutting societal satire about space — but that doesn't mean there aren't GTA-adjacent sci-fi adventures set in outer space. The frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet. Non-linear games set in outer space tend to be either too ambitious, like No Man's Sky, or too focused on specific experiences like space combat, like Star Wars: Squadrons. The end result is a roster of great sandboxes that let us journey to different star systems, but no game that dares to explore a criminal fantasy with the level of depth and opportunities seen in the last few Rockstar games. With new hardware powering far more complex open-world games, it's only a matter of time before "GTA in space" is a real thing. For now, there are some space games that let us explore sci-fi worlds, roleplaying as criminals and outlaws amongst the stars. Roleplaying a space outlaw (Image credit: Bethesda Softworks) Massive space RPGs like Starfield and The Outer Worlds 2 offer vast playgrounds you can explore and redefine through your actions. The lawful path is the obvious choice if you'd like to save the galaxy, but a life of crime awaits those who tire of the heroics. Starfield even has a "new game plus" mechanic baked into the player's journey, encouraging experimentation and living different lives, so if you stick with the divisive space RPG, the criminal life is all but unavoidable. And in traditional Bethesda fashion, you're not rushed to the next "main" objective, so if you want to become the most dangerous space criminal in the Settled Systems, you'll be supported by the mechanics and systems. You can always get back to saving the galaxy when you feel like it. (Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) The Outer Worlds 2 is another option if you want to become a star-surfing scoundrel. It might not be as absurdly expansive as Starfield, but Obsidian's whole deal has always been freedom of choice and roleplaying, so you can bet this humorous sequel also lets the protagonist become a bit of an a-hole. The main story already sets you in a collision course with corporate interests, too. Like in Mass Effect and other classic space RPGs, it's your choice to be either a goody-two-shoes or an edgy maniac, and I won't lie: the second option is usually more entertaining. Last but not least, there's a third game that also has enough going on to support a GTA-inspired fantasy in outer space: No Man's Sky . It's grown so much over the years that its original space exploration premise has been buried by content like fully customizable space stations, actual cities and towns

science.title: Trouble at Mars: NASA's Perseverance rover, Odyssey orbiter halt science work due to glitches
science.description: null Two of NASA's Mars explorers are sidelined by glitches at the moment. The Perseverance rover and Mars Odyssey orbiter have stood down from science work due to technical problems, NASA announced on Thursday (Nov. 19). Perseverance has been sidelined by an antenna issue, and the venerable Odyssey is dealing with a balky reaction wheel. NASA hopes both can get back to work at Mars by the end of November. Communication issues for Perseverance Perseverance landed inside Mars' Jezero Crater in February 2021, tasked with assessing the area's potential to support past life and with collecting dozens of samples for future return to Earth. It has done all this and more. The Perseverance team has determined that Jezero hosted a potentially habitable lake billions of years ago. And the car-sized rover has found a wealth of complex organic compounds in Martian rock, some of which might themselves be signs of life (though assessing this hypothesis fully will likely require bringing Perseverance's samples to Earth for analysis, scientists stress). In addition, Perseverance just set a new distance record for off-Earth driving, rolling past the mark set by its smaller cousin, NASA's Opportunity rover (28.06 miles, or 45.16 kilometers). Perseverance broke that record on Oct. 11. Just 19 days later, however, the mission team noticed a problem: The rover's main UHF downlink radio — which it uses to send information home to Earth, via data-relay satellites in Mars orbit — failed to send its usual "heartbeat" pings to the main computer. Perseverance detected this problem autonomously and reacted as it was programmed to do: The six-wheeled robot switched to its backup UHF radio and went into a protective "safe mode," shutting down all non-essential systems. The rover team recovered Perseverance from safe mode but soon noticed another issue: "The backup UHF radio was transmitting at about half of its expected power output," NASA officials wrote in an update on Thursday . Perseverance's handlers have stopped using that backup radio as well; the rover is now communicating with Earth directly (without the help of relay orbiters), sending signals to NASA's Deep Space Network dishes via its high-gain antenna. This pathway features lower data rates, and the mission team wants to prioritize the delivery of diagnostic information. So they've paused Perseverance's science work, which includes observations by its various cameras. The glitch may be disappointing to devoted Perseverance fans, many of whom have already noticed that the mission website hasn't uploaded any new raw images since Nov. 7 . But there's no reason to panic, according to NASA. "The rover is stable and communicating with the team," agency officials wrote in Thursday's update. "The team is hopeful the rover could return to science by the end of November, and NASA will provide further updates in the future as the team works the issue." science.title: There's an impostor hiding in the Hyades star cluster. Can you spot it?
science.description: null For years I looked at Taurus and saw something perfectly sensible. There was the Hyades, the big V-shaped cluster that forms the bull's face, with Aldebaran, noticeably brighter and more orange than the other stars, the dominant star. Every diagram reinforced the arrangement — Aldebaran was the eye of Taurus, the Hyades made the face, and in my head they became one object. Then I discovered that Aldebaran has nothing to do with the Hyades. I remember going outside afterward and looking again, half expecting the deception to become obvious now that I knew. It didn't. Aldebaran still looked completely at home among the other stars . The difference is hidden in the one dimension our eyes judge poorly when we look into space — depth. Aldebaran is about 65 light-years away, while the Hyades are roughly 150 light-years distant. The orange eye of Taurus is a foreground star that happens to lie almost exactly along our line of sight toward the Hyades. This fact exposes one of the most convincing tricks in stargazing. The night sky looks flat, and our brains are extremely willing to believe it. But it has incredible depth — and when you can see parts of the night sky in 3D, that's when you begin to appreciate that you're not looking at a flat map. Instead, you begin to see our cosmic neighborhood as it really is. By appreciating depth, you learn its geography. What's happening and when to look Aldebaran, the brightest star in the constellation of Taurus. (Image credit: Christophe Lehenaff via Getty Images) Taurus is now easy to find from the Northern Hemisphere during the evening. Once it's dark, look east for a small, tight knot of stars — the Pleiades open cluster (M45) — and then look nearby for a much larger V-shaped arrangement. That V is the Hyades, with unmistakably orange Aldebaran apparently sitting on one arm. Aldebaran's name is derived from the Arabic Al Dabarān, meaning "the follower," because it appears to trail the Pleiades across the night sky. The Hyades is a real physical group of stars — an open cluster — that formed together and moves through our galaxy together. About 153 light-years away, the Hyades is the nearest open star cluster to Earth. The name means "the rainmakers" because their rising and setting times in the ancient Greek sky coincided with wet weather. The stars in the Hyades are of a similar age — and mostly sun-like stars, or similar — so astronomers can tell that they all formed together in the same nebula . Orange-red star Aldebaran — the 14th-brightest star in the night sky — is the interloper, sitting less than half as far away from the sun . If you could somehow view the neighborhood from another part of the Milky Way , the familiar arrangement would fall apart. science.title: Could an ancient solar eclipse rewrite Egyptian history?
science.description: null The solar system is a clock that can be run in both directions. On Aug. 2, 2027, that clock will bring the moon's dark central shadow — a path of totality — back to Egypt. A t otal solar eclipse will sweep across the country , passing directly over Luxor and plunging some of ancient Egypt's greatest surviving monuments into darkness. Totality will begin in Luxor at approximately 1:02 p.m. EEST and last 6 minutes 22 seconds, according to Time and Date . We know when it will happen because we can calculate the motions of Earth and the moon centuries in advance. But run the same celestial clock backward and eclipses become one of nature's most precise timestamps. Astronomers can reconstruct where the moon's shadow fell thousands of years ago, even when nobody left a record of it. When an ancient text reliably describes an eclipse, it can anchor a moment in history to a specific place and time. Did an eclipse rewrite the Pyramid Age? Pharaoh Shepseskaf's huge rectangular tomb at South Saqqara (Image credit: Jon Bodsworth - www.egyptarchive.co.uk) We know from astronomical calculations that eclipses crossed Egypt long before anyone left an identifiable written record of one. On April 1, 2471 B.C., a total solar eclipse swept across northern Egypt during the age of the great pyramid builders. In research published in 2025, archaeoastronomer Giulio Magli at the Polytechnic University of Milan proposed that the eclipse may help explain why Pharaoh Shepseskaf broke with tradition and built a huge rectangular tomb at South Saqqara instead of a pyramid. It's a tantalizing hypothesis, but no surviving Egyptian text records the eclipse. Astronomers can calculate that an eclipse happened, but using it as a historical timestamp requires evidence that someone actually saw it and recorded it. That's where an eclipse almost 1,300 years later becomes particularly intriguing. Is the oldest recorded eclipse hidden in the Bible? Researchers have proposed that an annular eclipse occurred over Canaan on Oct. 30, 1207 BC, and may be described in the Bible. science.title: Russia is developing a nuclear space weapon, US intelligence report finds
science.description: null Last month, the U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) released a chilling and info-packed report judging the scope and breadth of threats posed by the nation's adversaries in space. The new report focuses on China , Russia and the emerging space powers of Iran and North Korea. It looks at what's happening in Earth orbit and beyond, including cislunar space, the region between our planet and the moon . The report — the 2026 edition of "Challenges to Security in Space" — is the third iteration of the DIA's unclassified intelligence assessment on space-related challenges and threats to U.S. national security, as well as the extent to which space is treated internationally as a warfighting domain . Information within the report, which you can read here , is current as of July 2026. DIA's mission is to provide intelligence on foreign militaries to help prevent wars, and win the ones that are fought. Up-front finding The report's up-front finding is that China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea are developing, testing, deploying and using space capabilities "in a way that threatens the security of all space systems and their associated space benefits." Indeed, China and Russia are developing "a formidable spectrum" of offensive capabilities to degrade or destroy space services of other countries, from kinetic destruction to sophisticated jamming and cyber operations. The DIA report also notes that "the production of cheaper, smaller, and simpler satellites , which are faster to develop and deploy, along with the expansion of commercially available launch services, are driving the rapid integration of commercial space alternatives to support national security." While space commercialization is making previously government-centered space services widely available to interested parties, the DIA report adds, that availability also includes state and non-state actors with malign interests. There are a range of threats to space-based services, both commercial and military. Some are reversible, while others are not. (Image credit: DIA) Counterspace worries A major item dealt with by the DIA is "counterspace" — and it's not the kind that you'll find in your kitchen. Counterspace operations can be either offensive or defensive. They can be used on purpose to reversibly or irreversibly deny, disrupt, degrade, damage or destroy a space object or component of a space system. Here are the key elements of counterspace, as identified within the DIA report: Antisatellite (ASAT) missiles are designed to kinetically strike and destroy satellites. ASAT missiles could produce massive amounts of debris that can remain in orbit for decades or even centuries. The Riemann hypothesis was first put forward in 1859 by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann. It proposes an origin for the prime numbers, namely that they follow a certain pattern. The question is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize Problems, which will award a $1 million prize for an accepted solution. Read more OpenAI has dumped 722 maths papers – now it must clean up the mess Levent Alpöge at Anthropic published a statement today claiming to have solved the problem with the aid of Anthropic’s Claude AI. Advertisement “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann hypothesis,” writes Alpöge. “It is natural to feel that this is an end, in my case a loss of a principal guiding light, but what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater.” In August, Anthropic announced previous work on the Riemann hypothesis , but that stopped short of a full proof. Alpöge hasn’t published a human-readable version of the proof, saying it would be “obviously inappropriate to attempt to post some massive unreadable travesty of ‘slop'”, though he says an unpublished version ran to more than 250,000 pages. Instead, Alpöge has released a version of the proof written in Lean, a computer code mathematicians use to mechanically verify proofs as a series of logical steps in a process called formalisation. science.title: ISS astronauts look down on the snow-capped Himalayas | Space photo of the day for Nov. 20, 2026
science.description: null A snapshot of the Himalayas captured from aboard the ISS. (Image credit: CSA/Joshua Kutryk) The Himalayas tower below the clouds, capped in icy snow in new snapshots captured from aboard the International Space Station . What is it? Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk was looking out one of the windows aboard the space station when the most incredible view came into focus — and thankfully he had a camera handy and was able to capture these striking scenes of the Himalayas from space. Above the mountain range, fluffy clouds hang in the atmosphere. Below, the expansive Himalayas are covered in bright snow and ice, which looks somehow both white and blue at the same time as the bright sunlight streaks across the breathtaking expanse. This frosty winter scene showcases the mountain range from orbit, from about 250 miles (400 kilometers) above Earth's surface. But even from this distance, the magnitude of this mountain range is palpable. The Himalayas stretch across five different countries including Nepal, India, China, Bhutan and Pakistan. And the Himalayas include some of the highest mountain peaks on planet Earth, including Mount Everest. Himalayas 🗻 https://t.co/IzGzu20H4Q November 17, 2026 Why is it incredible? From orbit around Earth, you might expect even the largest landmarks on our planet to appear miniscule. But somehow, in these photographs snapped by Kutryk during NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 mission , even from hundreds of miles above our planet you can really see and feel the immense scale of this mammoth mountain range. It's unclear exactly where above the mountain range these photographs were taken, but it is always amazing to think that within these sweeping landscapes are people living their lives, likely unaware that an astronaut is taking in the beauty of their home. Perhaps somewhere hidden under the clouds in one of Kutryk's photographs are hikers climbing up the side of Mt. Everest, completing their own bucket list adventure as the astronauts watching from above complete theirs.
